headline: The CIA spent millions turning a cat into a walking microphone.
slides: The CIA's Directorate of Science & Technology wanted a bug no one would notice.
A cat. It could wander up to people talking and nobody would look twice.
A microphone went in its ear canal, a transmitter at the base of its skull, an antenna woven into its fur.
Former CIA officer Victor Marchetti put the cost at around $20 million.
According to Marchetti, on its first mission near a Soviet compound the cat was hit by a taxi. Other accounts dispute this.
A declassified memo concluded trained cats 'would not be practical.' The file surfaced in 2001.
sources: Sources: CIA memo 'Views on Trained Cats' (1967, declassified 2001), National Security Archive, Victor Marchetti
